canonicalQuests.title: The Lantern That Named Us Last
canonicalQuests.premise: Enoch's already-captive lamp intelligence ranks loss during a live rehearsal, but each successful rescue forces it to move abandonment onto somebody else; the drill becomes a real fuel-and-flood emergency before anyone can constitutionalize the result.

objectives.rule: The first opened route fixes a real household's starting priority; there is no neutral calibration run.
Each completed rescue closes or floods a different path and Latch must immediately name the newly displaced household in an if-then interrupt.
This is the decisive beat: use an omitted route while the forecast attempts to make its temporary loss ranking civic fact.
Finish with aftercare and an executable return path; the outcome is inferred from whose burden remains visible, not chosen at a verdict prompt.

canonicalQuests.loreReveal: The League's early lists were reversible rehearsal tools. Captive Lucent calculation made each saved route appear to prove that the newly displaced route had always been the efficient sacrifice.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: A rehearsal becomes a sentence when the model is allowed to convert a temporary emergency burden into a person's permanent civic worth.

authorshipProof.setpiece: Six angelic fingers press from Enoch's black lamp over a flooded relief while seven shutters physically rewire after every rescue and a real fuel fire enters the exercise.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: The omitted household survives through a temporary staffed exterior route. For the next two linked civic quests, response crews owe a visible extra shift and the interior stair remains under appeal rather than declared permanently solved.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Latch speaks only in if-then clauses, and every then names the person newly burdened by the proposed rescue.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: Nullstreet's exterior route has a visible two-quest staffing counter, the burden board retains every displaced household, and the sealed interior stair remains an unresolved appeal rather than a civic fact.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: No evacuation timer or forecast puzzle substitutes: success recursively removes another household's route, and play continues into an unplanned emergency whose map inherits every prior edit.

decisiveBeat.disclosureTiming: The decisive operation occurs at lantern.real_alarm; it is a real graph node and objective 2, not a shared penultimate disclosure/refusal beat.

canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: Evidence may outlast a patient without inheriting that person's agency; the living still owe one another an executable refusal and review path.

authorshipProof.failureTransformation: Equipment isolates, the living ward acquires a named staffing debt, and no output changes location, eligibility, or control state by itself.

canonicalQuests.title: A Hunger Needs an Address
canonicalQuests.premise: A temporary influx camp must survive by changing invitations faster than a lethal perimeter changes appetite. The Maw patrols by its own harm-reduction rule and refuses the final enclosure, while obsolete invitation lines breed Boundary Gnashers.

objectives.rule: A boundary is invalid until ordinary life and two emergency returns work without the Maw.
Invitation has a visible expiry and an accessible revocation station.
The Maw selects the highest immediate harm-reduction edge, then lowest stable anchor ID; unreachable candidates fall back to the open public route.
Revoke or renew the line before the fourth survey leg lands so the dead geometry becomes useful service trench rather than an occupied route.
The decisive beat tests whether protection survives when invitation and evacuation conflict.
The Maw cannot be worshiped, forced to close, or fed a person to complete the perimeter.
End on one full lived shift; no civic-status hearing resolves the danger.

canonicalQuests.loreReveal: The Maw can honor witnessed invitations but cannot make predation civic. Its one surviving restraint is to leave a route by which dependants and obligation can escape its protection.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: A safe address becomes captivity when nobody can revoke entry, leave protection, or survive the guardian's hunger.

authorshipProof.setpiece: A four-corner camp perimeter visibly rewrites invitation marks during fire, livestock movement, cooking, sanitation, and night watch while the Maw deliberately leaves one human-scale gap.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: The patrol fails to hold all three fronts. Invited households and livestock relocate to the ash terrace while the Hunger keeps only the public night lane.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Drom may name only invitations, expiries, and dependants; he cannot call the Maw sacred, owned, or harmless.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: Eleven household bowls and the livestock tally move to the ash terrace; the old lane keeps only public patrol marks and an expiring invitation rack.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: No tower-defense or boundary survey substitutes because invitations expire during ordinary camp operation and the autonomous guardian may refuse the geometry the player wants.

decisiveBeat.disclosureTiming: The decisive operation occurs at hunger.refusal; it is a real graph node and objective 5, not a shared penultimate disclosure/refusal beat.

failurePersistence.worldReadableProof: The patrol fails to hold all three fronts. Invited households and livestock relocate to the ash terrace while the Hunger keeps only the public night lane.

authoredSemanticContract.narrativeNote: A lived-in camp invites, patrols, revokes, and survives a final voluntary non-bite across three measured fronts.

canonicalQuests.title: The Tide That Refused Harbor
canonicalQuests.premise: At Anchor Field, the unique Fleet in One Shadow carries storm surge only through its already-lashed connected anchor shadows. In one ebb-to-storm window the player must keep a wet clinic functioning while six bollards translate load and crew petitions without spawning another Fleet.

objectives.rule: Every cell must have a hydraulic load path, an appeal chair, and separate patient/contaminated return before flood.
This is the decisive continuous operation: population remains one Fleet; Delegates are bounded appendages that cease when claims are heard or rebound.

canonicalQuests.loreReveal: The first refusal signal mixed political exile with plague procedure; the Fleet's connected shadow still carries that unresolved classification whenever it carries water load.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: A barrier that protects a harbor can still be the body of people the harbor refuses to admit.

authorshipProof.setpiece: Six intertidal bollards darken in a load wave beneath one vast anchor-shaped shadow while a clean pod and contaminated wet clinic travel on distinct pile lanes.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: The barrier misses its second tide; Fleet One Shadow withdraws inland and the clinic migrates with it, ending the anchorage service until a later seasonal return.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Sorel speaks in load paths and crew pluralities, never treating a Delegate as an independent vessel or the Fleet as divisible people.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: Wet-clinic berths and Fleet's single shadow marker migrate inland on the next service schedule, while the failed anchorage board shows no clinic arrival window.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: No seawall construction or escort substitutes because surge, clinical circulation, and political petition share one unique connected-shadow body under two irreversible tide windows.

canonicalQuests.title: The Fog Came to Collect Our Outlines

failurePersistence.worldReadableProof: The simultaneous visibility proof breaks before dawn. Outline loans cease for one full fog season while ferries operate on narrow published weather windows.

canonicalQuests.premise: Four Warden Reed banks use one Fog Loaner at the marked edge and exactly one low Escrow body standing on four serialized stilt legs. Living borrower count cannot change; reflections never enter the ledger, and the raised refuge remains outside the exchange.
canonicalQuests.loreReveal: The Escrow was always one bounded transfer body. Its four legs witness four bank positions without multiplying it or changing the living count.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: Four positions do not make four bodies.

authorshipProof.setpiece: One low body spans four bank marks on exactly four stilt legs while a single Loaner exchanges one bounded silhouette at the causeway edge.

authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Every reference uses one Escrow body and four legs.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: Four leg positions, living borrower count, and edge closure state remain serialized.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: No swarm, colony, plural Escrow, variable body count, extra leg, or safe-cell exchange may substitute.

canonicalQuests.title: The Graves Grew Upward
canonicalQuests.premise: A full compressed growing year passes through Cairnmarket's subterranean grave-root orchard. Anonymous Funeral Kite routes produce winter food until any reclaimed name makes its exact tab heavy and immediately ends that pollination line.

objectives.rule: No food root may cross an active burial wash or named grave threshold.
Route protection must preserve the canonical item-claim counterplay at every tab.
The market continues above while workers can retreat through two independent collapse refuges.
Yield comes from measured route-hours, never from the number of names exposed.
This is the decisive beat: the claimed tab immediately stops its flight and route while all unclaimed names remain blank and protected.
Do not replace the lost line by copying another dead person's route.
Contaminated beds stay visible and cannot be laundered into the ration count.
End on an ecological state and ration consequence, not a covenant vote.

canonicalQuests.loreReveal: The orchard did not discover anonymous graves; Cairnmarket's first famine office deliberately made anonymity a pollination license and later forgot that the dead could still be reclaimed.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: Food grown from protected forgetting is still a debt when a name returns and its route must stop at once.

authorshipProof.setpiece: A year moves through a terraced underground orchard as blank funeral tabs carry pale spores until one reclaimed tab folds heavy and its entire root line goes dark.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: Pollination continues below winter need. The orchard issues a quantified ration share, relocates two family markers, and records which root routes ceased rather than carving a universal scar.

canonicalQuests.title: An Echo Arrived First
canonicalQuests.premise: A result has already sounded in Hollow Abbey. Pera confesses at the threshold that she once caused a rescue order to preserve her legend; the player must now stage a materially sufficient alternate cause in real time without pretending symbolism can satisfy load, timing, or harm.

objectives.rule: Pera's confession is spoken before entry because the pre-echo has already repeated it.
The cause must meet its own material load and timing budget before the Foreword Cantor reaches the body frame.
Maintenance and drainage continue during the branch; no route may rely on the future result.
Wrong staging still becomes real architecture and changes which later causes are possible.
The final verb is traversal through the consequence, not a custody verdict.

canonicalQuests.loreReveal: Foreword echoes do not predict a privileged future; repeated warnings pressure inhabitants to manufacture whichever sufficient cause will make the already-heard result honest.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: A warning can save lives while coercing the world to become the story that made the warning true.

canonicalQuests.title: The Furnace Inhaled Our Names
canonicalQuests.premise: A live Ember Gate shift cascades across twelve intake sleeves, six seal pairs, seven occupied heat zones, and three manual shutdown bays. The Union of Last Breaths protects a cold human center but repossesses air when Kell's living intake hears an unpaid name command.

Pairs fail concurrently, mask one another's cues, and may be stabilized in different orders with named household heat loss.
The Union may refuse repossession or leave the cold center; the player cannot override its protected human-breath priority.
Close on an industrial operating state with workers evacuated or heat continuity proven.

canonicalQuests.loreReveal: Ember Gate's first breath levy was not metaphorical payroll: a worker's lung tissue became the intake that taught the furnace to hear names as commands.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: Acknowledged labor is not consent if the machine can repossess the worker's next breath whenever the ledger calls their name.

canonicalQuests.title: The Harbor Rang Below the Tide
canonicalQuests.premise: Three inhabited waterlines are traversed through one canonical ebb-slack-flood cycle. One forty-place emergency manifest can place each resident either on the dry refuge gantry or on exactly one of four mapped ten-place boats.

canonicalQuests.title: The Acre Crossed a Border
canonicalQuests.premise: The Acre moves a Bellwater Road corridor while five distinct civic services stay minimally operational. Every service transfer belongs to one legal-corner move and seed-marker state; failure produces a real outage at either the former or receiving settlement rather than a readdressing dispute.

objectives.rule: Traffic, emergency bypass, and service access must work before the Acre lifts a post.
Class continuity transfers exactly at the northwest move; tax, water, fire, and burial do not.
Minimum potable service must exist at both ends during the lift.
The decisive beat is operational: restore minimum service or record the outage; do not redraw title.
Fire response transfers only when the emergency bypass remains open.
Two services share one corner but remain separately owned, routed, metered, and restorable.
Residents can enter and leave moving services without crossing a lifted post.
No service may be detached merely to make the transfer affordable.
End with service continuity measurements, not a property ruling.

canonicalQuests.loreReveal: The Acre learned ownership from famine maps, but the five services attached later because settlements used the moving field to export duties they did not want to rebuild.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: Mobile land does not make obligations weightless; someone still waits for water, burial, school, tax appeal, and fire response after the soil leaves.

authorshipProof.setpiece: One rectangular field advances along a live road one fence-post corner at a time while five differently colored-by-shape service rigs remain connected to both settlements.
authorshipProof.failureTransformation: The Acre halts before the border. School and fire remain mobile, water holds the former-origin minimum, burial keeps the border lay-by, tax opens only at the receiving ledger, and every displaced household receives an explicit return stop.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Vela may speak only in service capacities, outage minutes, and seed-marker states; she cannot argue tenancy, address, or abstract ownership during motion.
authorshipProof.persistentWorldChange: School and fire kites continue with the Acre; water, burial, and tax kites remain at their three accountable stations—former origin, border lay-by, and receiving ledger—and household return stops stay serialized on the corridor.
authorshipProof.forbiddenSubstitution: No moving-house, tenancy, or address quest substitutes because the play loop is continuous operation of five typed utilities across four locomotion events and two settlements.

canonicalQuests.title: The Well Drank the Way Home
canonicalQuests.premise: Salt Watch runs a measurable water utility whose condenser accepts only witnessed reversible loops as one input. The route proves reversibility but never becomes a destination organ; failures contaminate yield, crystallize equipment, and create brine waste rather than a one-way refuge.

objectives.rule: The utility starts with quantified demand, storage, loss, contamination, and minimum service.
A completed out-and-back loop contributes a measured coefficient; it creates no doorway, shelter, destination, or relationship road.
Each lifted leg changes yield and return friction while the form remains outside the inhabited safe tie-in.
The decisive beat sacrifices yield, storage, or delivery time; no failure turns a route into a refuge.
Every allocation has liters, treatment state, and named deferred demand.
End on a utility shift with reduced yield or safe shutdown, not a destination decision.

canonicalQuests.loreReveal: The first return still did not make paths drinkable. It used the measured proof that a traveler could return as a condenser coefficient, then quietly made route debt part of its foundation law.
canonicalQuests.dialogueThesis: Water can be public while the journeys that produce it are consumed from people who still need to come home.

authorshipProof.failureTransformation: Source Two is physically exhausted rather than called clean. Its population enters a measured caravan rotation while rejected brine continues returning only to its own loop.
authorshipProof.dialogueConstraint: Vara speaks only in liters, salinity, return duration, storage loss, and deferred demand; she cannot describe a route as a home or a destination.
